ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory for all partners, UBOs (>=25% ownership or control), directors and authorized signatories: (a) FINTRAC-aligned identity verification and beneficial-ownership determination; (b) screening against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the United Nations Consolidated List, the Canadian consolidated sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act list; (c) Politically Exposed Person (PEP) identification and Enhanced Due Diligence under PCMLTFA s. 9.3 and FINTRAC guidance, including family members and close associates; (d) adverse-media and negative-news review. Business-specific finding: the AI/LLM API platform billing via Stripe and USDC is rated Low_Risk_Standard; the LP is not a money services business or financial entity under PCMLTFA, and USDC acceptance constitutes the LP's own trade receivables rather than virtual-currency dealing, so no FINTRAC MSB registration is triggered.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) - filings processed through the Corporate Registry System (CORES) via approved registry agents and MyAlberta Digital ID; a NUANS Name Search Report is mandatory for all registrations
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Registered names must be in Latin script (English and/or French); a non-Latin brand name (e.g., Chinese) must be rendered in transliterated or translated Latin-script form; the name must contain a distinctive element plus a legal element (e.g., 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.') and must not be merely descriptive, misleading, or confusingly similar to an existing registered name
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: "Bank", "Banker", "Banking", "Trust", "Trust Company" - require prior consent of the federal/provincial financial regulator (OSFI or Alberta Treasury Board and Finance)
"Engineer", "Engineering" - require consent of the Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of Alberta (APEGA) under the Engineering and Geoscience Professions Act
"Lawyer", "Barrister", "Solicitor", "Legal Services" - require Law Society of Alberta authorization
"Doctor", "Medical", "Clinic", "Health Centre" - require health profession regulator consent
"Royal", "Crown", "Government", "Ministerial", "Commission", "Authority" - imply Crown or government affiliation and are restricted
"Alberta", "Canada" (used as leading geographic tokens) - restricted when implying governmental or misleading geographic association
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No statutory extension exists; if registration is not completed within the 90-day NUANS reservation validity window, a new name search and reservation must be filed. Upon rejection: (1) the registry agent communicates the written grounds of refusal; (2) the applicant amends the proposed name to eliminate the objectionable or confusing token and re-files through the same registry agent; (3) if a final refusal is maintained, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with Service Alberta Corporate Registry, and thereafter seek judicial review in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within 30 days of the final administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible: the LP must maintain a registered office at a physical street address within Alberta where court and registry documents can be served during normal business hours; a professional virtual-office or commercial registered-agent address is accepted, but a P.O. Box alone is non-compliant; the registered office may differ from head-office or operations locations for this internationally operating API platform.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (5-10%): Service Alberta conducts targeted address-verification and registry compliance audits; for a low-risk international AI/LLM API business using a professional commercial registered agent, the estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection is approximately 5-10%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, Part 2 (Limited Partnerships), as amended; and the Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9 (for the corporate general partner)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Registration of Limited Partnership form (Alberta Partnership Act, Form LP-1) together with executed Limited Partnership Agreement
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; nominal capital may be fixed by the Limited Partnership Agreement. Contributions are contractually governed and no escrow or capital deposit is required by the Alberta Partnership Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner of the Alberta limited partnership approves the Limited Partnership Agreement dated [DATE], and that the General Partner hereby subscribes for its agreed partnership interest on behalf of the partnership. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the partnership's registered office shall be at the address set forth in the Registration of Limited Partnership, and that [NAME] is appointed as the initial general partner representative, with full authority to execute and file the registration, open bank accounts, engage auditors, and complete all ancillary filings. All lawful acts incidental to formation are hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (NUANS Name Search issued via accredited service providers)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS search for the proposed limited partnership name, review conflicting corporate and trade names, and submit a name reservation through an Alberta Corporate Registry agent to secure the name for 90 days
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report
Name reservation request form
Consent to name usage (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or conflicts with an existing registration, submit a revised name or written justification to the Corporate Registry; a new NUANS report may be required

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private legal counsel; no government filing at this stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a Limited Partnership Agreement among the general partner and limited partners, setting capital contributions, profit-sharing, management authority, transfer restrictions, dissolution events, and indemnification terms
required_dossiers: Draft Limited Partnership Agreement
Consent and power of attorney executed by all partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: No government remedy required; partners may amend the agreement by mutual consent and execute a restated agreement

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (online via Registry Agents or Corporate Registry services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the Registration of Limited Partnership form, including the registered office address in Alberta, the name and address of the general partner, and the executed power of attorney for service of process; pay the prescribed filing fee at submission
required_dossiers: Completed Registration of Limited Partnership form (Form LP-1)
Certified copy of the Limited Partnership Agreement
Consent of the general partner and initial registered office
Power of attorney for service (for each non-resident general partner)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for incomplete information, the registry will issue a deficiency notice; cure by filing an amended declaration within the stated period and re-pay any applicable reactivation fee

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Registration and Alberta Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful filing, the registry issues a Certificate of Registration evidencing the limited partnership; the CRA assigns a federal Business Number upon filing an initial registration return or through the CRA Business Registration Online portal
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration from Alberta Corporate Registry
CRA Business Registration Information
General partner identification and residency details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry delays issuance, escalate through Service Alberta registry support; if the CRA business number application is queried, correct the information at CRA Business Registration Online or contact CRA individual business accounts

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration, and Workers' Compensation Board – Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the partnership for GST/HST (if taxable sales exceed C$30,000), provincial employer health tax (if applicable), and WCB account; obtain import/export program accounts if applicable to cross-border service delivery
required_dossiers: CRA GST/HST registration form
Alberta corporate income tax notice
WCB account registration application
General partner corporate registry profile
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax or WCB application is rejected, correct discrepancies identified in the rejection letter and re-file; late registration penalties may be waived under CRA voluntary disclosure procedures for inadvertent omissions

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Governance Minutes, Operating Bank Account, and Share Capital Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first organizational meeting of the general partner, adopt the required board resolutions, maintain partnership minute books, issue general partner director/officer consents, and open a segregated partnership bank account requiring authorized signatory confirmation
required_dossiers: Certified board resolution of the general partner
Partnership Agreement and Certificate of Registration
Directors' and officers' consent forms
Bank account onboarding forms and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank documentation is rejected for insufficient evidence, provide a Canadian bank-issued or notarized copy of the Certificate of Registration and updated beneficial ownership registry

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 6201 generative AI API platform is a digital-service activity with no manufacturing plant or physical industrial operation
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required under Alberta industrial licensing statutes for AI/LLM API platform operations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical construction, discharge point, or environmental disturbance; applicable only if a data center or physical premises exceeds municipal development thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If office or data infrastructure is established, comply with Alberta's Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (SSB limits), municipal wastewater sewer-use bylaws, and provincial VOC/electronic-waste disposal regulations for server hardware and cooling equipment

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code and municipal fire department occupancy inspection for the registered office; compliance with Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Act for workplace ergonomics, electrical safety, server-room fire suppression, and emergency evacuation procedures

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Agence du revenu du Canada) — official national portal: Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account; Alberta counterpart for LP/registry compliance: Alberta Corporate Registry and Alberta Finance and Treasury Board / Tax and Revenue Administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canada does not issue a standalone TIN/VAT ID; the CRA Business Number (BN) is the statutory tax identifier and the GST/HST program account (BN ending in RT0001) is the VAT ID. An Alberta LP obtains the BN as follows: (1) file the Declaration of Limited Partnership with the Alberta Corporate Registry (or extra-provincial registration if formed outside Alberta) and obtain the Alberta entity number; (2) file Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) through CRA Business Registration Online, using the non-resident registration route and attaching a certified certificate of existence/good standing for every foreign partner or foreign LP; (3) declare the intended GST/HST registration, available ITC activity, and Canadian place of business/proposed permanent establishment; (4) receive from CRA the BN and activate the GST/HST account; (5) if non-resident partners will receive Canadian-source income, open the applicable Part XIII/Part I withholding account; and (6) maintain the BN, Alberta registry number, and foreign TINs in the required CRA books and records for at least six years.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the Alberta limited partnership is fiscally transparent for federal and Alberta income tax; the partnership files no entity-level income tax (a T5013 information return is filed only for allocation reporting) and each partner reports allocated shares of income/loss. For GST/HST purposes the partnership is a separate statutory person and may be a small supplier or mandatory/voluntary registrant; this indirect-tax status does not alter direct-tax pass-through treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Canadian analogue to the U.S. check-the-box election exists, and an Alberta LP cannot elect to be taxed as a corporation. The principal elections relevant to this structure are: (i) voluntary GST/HST registration election under section 240(2) of the Excise Tax Act if below the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold; (ii) partnership fiscal-period election and partner fiscal-period alignment elections under the Income Tax Act; and (iii) certain Alberta Corporate Registry elections regarding extra-provincial registration. Hybrid mismatch rules in the Income Tax Act apply automatically and do not offer a check-the-box or elective remedial mechanism; no election is available to avoid hybrid mismatch adjustments.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) together with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) in a prudential supervisory role, and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/CTF enforcement under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). The federal Bank Act, SC 1991, c. 46, and the Canadian Payments Act govern clearing and settlement, while provincial securities regulators (Alberta Securities Commission) and the Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA) monitor stablecoin dealings that may constitute securities or derivatives.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current and capital account; Canada accepts Article VIII obligations of the IMF and observes the OECD Codes of Liberalisation. No central bank approval, exchange permit, or capital account certificate is required for capital contributions, foreign revenue remittances, loan repayments, or distributions to non-resident limited partners of an Alberta Limited Partnership. Operational frictions are limited to: (i) Part XIII withholding tax at 25% on allocated income distributions to non-resident partners unless reduced by treaty (with appropriate NR3016/NR302 forms); (ii) FINTRAC large-value transaction reporting by financial intermediaries for any cross-border electronic funds transfer of CAD 10,000 or more; and (iii) bank-level source-of-funds verification where inflows originate from crypto-assets such as USDC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no mandatory surrender, no repatriation window, and no statutory conversion ratio on export proceeds or AI API service fees. USD, EUR, or multi-currency balances may be retained indefinitely in corporate treasury accounts. The only compliance element is transactional: every cross-border wire at or above CAD 10,000 executed through a Canadian financial institution must generate a large cross-border currency transaction report filed with FINTRAC, requiring the LP to maintain accurate originator and beneficiary details and a substantiated purpose code.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium-High for merchant collections and fast FX conversion; Low for primary treasury custody, escrow, or capital subscription banking. Legal constraints: offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, Airwallex, Payoneer, and Mercury are not 'banks' under the Bank Act and cannot offer Canadian deposit-taking, CDIC insurance, or direct Lynx RTGS settlement. They must register as Money Service Businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC if they service Canadian clients. Deposits held with such EMIs are not CDIC-insured and may be subject to segregated client money rules, which are inadequate for LP capital escrow. Recommended structure: maintain the Schedule I bank treasury anchor for all capital and tax-sensitive flows; use a FINTRAC-registered EMI exclusively as a 26-market collection sleeve for token receipts, with automated daily sweeps of funds to the primary bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permitted in Canada; no statute in the Bank Act or PCMLTFA requires a mandatory physical branch visit. In practice, Schedule I banks require a video identity interview with each director, the general partner, or any 25% beneficial owner. For an Alberta LP with foreign limited partners, banks will require: (i) the executed LP Agreement and Declaration of Partnership; (ii) Alberta Corporate Registry extract showing the Corporate Access Number and registered office; (iii) passport and proof of residential address for all KYC principals; (iv) a certified corporate register of the general partner; (v) a Treasury Authorization Letter; and (vi) for a foreign corporate GP, apostilled constitutional documents and board resolutions. Enhanced due diligence will be triggered if any principal is resident in a high-risk jurisdiction or if source-of-wealth documentation is incomplete; in those cases a physical visit to a Canadian or correspondent branch may be required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign ownership concentration: >25% of the LP is held by non-resident limited partners in Asia or EMEA without a Canadian economic nexus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Corporate Registry Certificate plus consolidated beneficial-ownership schedule identifying all 25%+ holders; executed LP Agreement with capital commitment schedule; passport pages and proof of residential address for each natural person; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; Canadian registered office lease and corporate agent appointment; explanation of the LP's business connection to Alberta.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: USDC stablecoin treasury inflows and outflows triggering digital-asset AML red flags at the bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: USDC handling policy restricted to FINTRAC-registered crypto trading platforms or securities-registered OTC desks; executed settlement agreements with liquidity providers; one-to-one reserve ledger; whitelisted wallet addresses without mixing services; blockchain analytics compliance reports; prohibition of high-risk crypto counterparties and tumbling.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unregulated generative AI/LLM business scope with limited traceability of API customers and outputs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: NAICS 541511 / ISIC 6201 classification memorandum; technical whitepaper on the LLM inference product; standard API terms with acceptable-use and AI safety clauses; model red-teaming attestation; privacy impact assessment; customer due-diligence procedures including PEP and sanctions screening; data residency explanation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wires in excess of CAD 10,000 with wedge-shaped USD inflows matched by rapid outbound disbursements to cloud providers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month projected revenue and cash-flow model; transaction subledger matched to GPU compute consumption in AWS/Azure; master service agreements with hyperscale cloud vendors; board-approved treasury and FX hedging policy; audit trail tracing each wire to the relevant customer settlement and compute invoice.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance deficiency: LP treated as a 'brass plate' entity administered solely from a registered agent office without Alberta operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Calgary office lease in the LP name; Canadian-resident general partner declaration; Alberta Business Number registration and municipal business license; evidence of Alberta-based technical staff or dependent agents; intellectual-property ownership or development commitments localized in Alberta; management accounts showing payroll and operating expenditure; economic-substance letter aligned with OECD BEPS standards.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign limited partner capital injections must be routed by SWIFT MT202/MT103 to the LP's designated Capital Escrow Account at a Schedule I bank, referencing the specific subscription agreement and capital call number in the remittance narrative. The LP must provide a capital contributions register and source-of-funds letters. For USD contributions, funds may be held in a USD suspense account and converted to CAD via a spot contract, or retained for direct payment of USD-denominated cloud compute costs. For USDC-denominated capital, the contribution must be liquidated through a FINTRAC-registered Canadian crypto dealer or a securities-regulated OTC desk into CAD/USD and then wired to the bank; the bank will require a chain-of-ownership report evidencing wallet origin and absence of mixers. No CRA approval is required for capital additions, but each partner's capital account must be properly recorded to support T5013 and any future NR4 withholding calculations. For inbound wires from Stripe payouts, the routing benefit code should reflect 'computer and information services' to enable clean reconciliation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement rails for the AI API platform: (i) core cloud and software subscriptions (AWS, Azure, Databricks) are paid via SWIFT MT103 gpi with UETR from the operating account using ISO 20022 purpose code 'PROC' (computer services processing); (ii) Canadian vendor invoices under CAD 1 million use Payments Canada EFT/ACH same-day rails; (iii) the Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) is reserved only for procurement of GPU servers or HPC hardware from third-party OEMs where trade credit is required; (iv) USDC payouts to overseas compute providers are made exclusively via licensed custodial wallets and settled through a FINTRAC-registered exchange, converting USDC to USD/CAD before sweeping to the bank; (v) Stripe card settlement is remitted in USD to the bank's USD account by SWIFT, with a standing instruction to auto-convert and sweep balances into the CAD treasury account daily. Each disbursement is matched against a compute-usage subledger and must be accompanied by a documented invoice to satisfy CRA transfer-pricing and GST/HST input-credit requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Spot Contracts (T+2 USD/CAD settlement; executable under a standard Treasury Authorization Letter; used for operational conversion of Stripe and USDC proceeds)

Outright FX Forwards (1M to 12M tenors; documented under the International Foreign Exchange and Options Master Agreement (IFEMA) or a bank's Canadian Master Forward Agreement; used to lock conversion of recurring USD API revenue into CAD operating currency)

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) (permissible for restricted-currency counterparties such as INR, CNY, or KRW where offshore deliverability is limited; requires an ISDA Master Agreement with the bank or a licensed international NDF broker; no settlement of the restricted currency occurs, only the USD difference)

Cross-Currency Swaps (XCCY) (permissible for structural matching of long-dated USD compute leases against USD revenue; documented under an ISDA Master Agreement with a Credit Support Annex (CSA); used where debt-funded GPU capacity exceeds a 2-year horizon)

European-Style FX Options (USD/CAD calls and puts; permissible for hedging uncertain revenue conversion; requires a board-approved hedging policy, bank suitability assessment, and premium recording in the LP's financial statements; prohibited for speculative use under the Alberta Partnership Act fiduciary rules)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not generally required for an Alberta limited partnership. File amendments promptly when registered particulars change, including partners, registered office, or partnership name.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No routine annual-return penalty or automatic administrative strike-off applies solely because an Alberta limited partnership has no annual return requirement. Failure to maintain or amend registration may impair good standing and may lead to registry action after notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Information Return (Form T5013), if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due within five months after the partnership fiscal year-end when the partnership is required to file under the Income Tax Act, including common cases involving corporate or trust partners, non-resident partners, 50 or more partners, or prescribed financial thresholds.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties may be assessed at CAD 25 per day, subject to statutory minimum and maximum amounts, commonly up to CAD 2,500. Repeated non-compliance may trigger CRA enforcement, reassessment, or a demand to file; no Alberta corporate strike-off follows from a T5013 omission.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general Alberta or Canadian statutory independent-audit requirement applies solely because the entity is a limited partnership. An audit may be required by the partnership agreement, financing documents, investors, securities-law obligations, or applicable tax and regulatory circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian accounting standards for private enterprises are generally applicable where financial statements are prepared for a private partnership. IFRS may be adopted by agreement or required by investors, lenders, or applicable regulatory circumstances. Tax reporting follows Canadian federal income-tax rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No general public beneficial-ownership annual confirmation or annual UBO filing applies to an Alberta limited partnership. Maintain current partner, ownership-interest, transfer, contribution, control, and beneficial-owner records under the partnership agreement and applicable AML/KYC rules. Record transfers in accordance with the partnership agreement and file registry amendments when legally required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Certificate and registration particulars of the limited partnership
Register of general and limited partners
Register of partnership interests, transfers, and capital contributions
Minutes or written resolutions of partners
Beneficial-ownership and control records maintained for applicable AML/KYC purposes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 400-1,200 per year, depending on service scope, document forwarding, compliance reminders, and nominee or local-contact services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000-12,000 where an audit is contractually or commercially required; otherwise USD 0 for a statutory audit not mandated by law.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (pass-through entity; Limited Partnerships in Canada are not subject to entity-level corporate income tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: None at entity level; flow-through taxation to partners with potential small business deduction eligibility for partners

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T3 Return of Income for a Partnership (filed electronically via CRA My Account or NETFILING)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 90 days after the end of the fiscal year for T3 filing; partners must file personal T1 returns by April 30 (June 15 for some provinces)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate income of the partnership including business income from AI services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners receive T5013 slip; allocate income per partnership agreement

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net business income from operations including LLM API services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Income allocated to non-resident partners reported on T5013; no entity tax

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions such as capital cost allowance for AI infrastructure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions flow through to partners for their tax calculations

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T3 filing: $50 per day to a maximum of $1,000; failure to provide T5013 slips: penalties; unpaid partner tax: interest and 10% penalty

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: N/A (distributions from LP not subject to withholding tax; income tax paid by partners)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident partners claim applicable treaty benefits on T5013; no TRC required for partnership distributions; report foreign tax credits if applicable
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest payments to non-residents: 25% statutory rate, reduced by tax treaty (typically 0-15%); Royalties: 10% statutory, reduced by treaty (0-10%)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: $500,000 CAD (triggers mandatory transfer pricing documentation for related-party transactions exceeding this threshold)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Not applicable; Canadian tax authorities apply General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and substance-over-form principles to assess economic reality

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate failure to report or underreport partnership income or false statements on T3 or T5013
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction with fines up to $100,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties and interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners in LP may have unlimited liability; all partners personally liable for taxes, penalties, and potential jail time

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing or maintaining an LP without genuine business purpose or economic substance solely for tax avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment disallowing deductions; penalties of 25-50% of tax benefit; possible criminal charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil; partners face personal liability for unpaid taxes, interest, and prosecution

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register with FINTRAC, implement AML policies, or report suspicious transactions related to AI API payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to $10,000 per violation; possible license suspension or criminal liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior officers and partners personally liable for fines and potential imprisonment for willful non-compliance
